summary: Generic crystalline derived monodromy for decent acceptable pairs, the finite-extension open-image point, central lifting, and a final component/converse consumer. The arithmetic proof uses corrected Galois-orbit minima, full monodromy before taking identity components, and compact Galois-orbit descent. Generic-filtration and ADLV supplier gaps remain explicit; this is a complete planning pass, not a closed or implemented theory.

nodes.title: The jump of a nonzero filtered vector
nodes.statement: For a field K, a K-vector space V and a decreasing, exhaustive and separated integer filtration F, DegreeAt(F,v,d) means v ∈ F^d and v ∉ F^(d+1). Every nonzero v has a unique such integer. The predicate itself is defined for any family of submodules; existence and uniqueness require the filtration hypotheses. No integer degree is assigned to zero.
hypotheses: K is a field; V is a K-vector space. The filtration is bounded above and below for the existence assertion.
proofSteps: Define DegreeAt by membership and nonmembership in the existing Submodule carrier.
For v ≠ 0, the set of indices containing v is a nonempty proper lower subset of the integers; its largest member is the required jump. Antitonicity proves uniqueness.
acceptance: A rank-one filtration jumping at a gives degree a, including negative a.
Zero has no jump, even though it belongs to every submodule.

sources.match: The degree is the unique jump of a nonzero vector for a decreasing filtration.

uses.how: Sum the jumps of successive Frobenius translates.
Compare the actual jump with the imported generic-filtration threshold.

nodes.title: The full-period Frobenius degree sum
nodes.statement: For a set X of nonzero vectors, a degree d:X→ℤ and a self-map φ:X→X, frobeniusDegreeSum(d,φ,s,v)=Σ_{0≤i<s} d(φ^i(v)). In the crystalline application X is the nonzero subtype of V⊗F, φ=ρ(b)σ is bijective, s>0 is a decency period, and d is the μ-filtration jump over K. The summands need not be equal.
hypotheses: s is a natural number; positivity is required only in the arithmetic application.
proofSteps: Take the finite sum over Finset.range s, using ordinary iteration.
Instantiate the nonzero subtype using bijectivity of the isocrystal Frobenius; extend vectors to K only to evaluate the filtration.
acceptance: For s=0 the sum is 0; no division by s occurs in this definition.
For a two-cycle with degrees 1 and -1, the full-period sum is 0.

sources.match: The sum follows the entire s-step semilinear orbit.

uses.how: Turn s inertia bounds into the full Galois average.

api.name: frobeniusDegreeSum_zero
api.statement: The sum for period zero equals 0.

api.name: frobeniusDegreeSum_one
api.statement: The sum for period one equals d(v).

api.name: frobeniusDegreeSum_succ
api.statement: The (s+1)-sum is the s-sum plus d(φ^s(v)).

api.name: frobeniusDegreeSum_map
api.statement: A map intertwining φ and ψ and preserving degrees preserves all full-period sums.

tests.name: degreeSum_zero
tests.statement: A zero-length orbit has sum 0 for every degree function.

tests.name: degreeSum_fixed
tests.statement: For φ=id, the sum equals s·d(v).

tests.name: degreeSum_unequalCycle

tests.name: degreeSum_not_firstJump

nodes.title: Vectors satisfying the Newton and Hodge equations
nodes.statement: Fix an s-decent b, s>0, K/F finite, a filtration μ and a rational representation ρ:G→GL(V). For k∈ℤ let V^{s,k}_{b,μ} be the set of nonzero v∈V⊗Q_p Q_{p^s} for which ρ((sν_b)(p))v=p^k v and d_s(v)=k. This is a set, not a declared subspace. The Frobenius sum is computed in V⊗F, where F=breve Q_p.
hypotheses: b and ν_b descend to Q_{p^s}; sν_b is integral.
All degree summands are evaluated on nonzero vectors using the μ-filtration over K.
proofSteps: Use the imported decency identity to define the Newton operator on V⊗Q_{p^s}.
Intersect its nonzero p^k-eigenvectors with the level set k of the degree sum; do not close under addition.
acceptance: Neither the zero vector nor a vector satisfying only the Newton equation belongs automatically.

sources.match: The two equations jointly pick the coefficient lines used by the crystalline Tannakian group.

uses.how: Parameterize rank-one coefficient subobjects by their fibre lines.
Extract the Newton slope k/s for all occurring torus weights.

api.name: newtonHodgeVectors_mem
api.statement: Membership is equivalent to nonzero, the Newton eigenvalue equation, and the Hodge equality.

api.name: newtonHodgeVectors_smul
api.statement: Multiplication by Q_{p^s}^× preserves membership and the represented line.

api.name: newtonHodgeVectors_tensorMap
api.statement: A representation morphism preserving the filtered isocrystal sends a member to a member with the same k whenever its image is nonzero.

tests.name: newtonHodge_rankOne
tests.statement: For φ=p^aσ and μ of weight h, a nonzero rational vector belongs to V^{s,k} exactly when k=sa=sh.

tests.name: newtonHodge_zeroExcluded
tests.statement: For the zero representation every V^{s,k} is empty.

tests.name: newtonHodge_wrongHodge

tests.name: newtonHodge_cyclicCoefficient
tests.statement: For the coefficient object with jumps d_i and wrap p^k, its distinguished cyclic vector belongs exactly when Σ_i d_i=k.

nodes.title: The finite decent-field crystalline fibre functor
nodes.statement: On the full tensor subcategory of isocrystals whose slopes have denominators dividing s, define ω_s(N)=⊕_λ {x∈N_λ | φ^s(x)=p^{sλ}x}, a Q_{p^s}-vector space. This is an exact faithful tensor functor, with ω_s(N)⊗_{Q_{p^s}}F≅N. Restrict it to the subcategory C_{b,μ} generated by F_{b,μ}(Rep G), closed under subquotients. If b is s-decent, its composite with F_{b,μ} identifies canonically with V↦V⊗Q_{p^s}; hence the full group H_cris,s=Aut^⊗(ω_s|C_{b,μ}) embeds in G_{Q_{p^s}}.
hypotheses: s>0 clears the slopes of a faithful representation, and therefore all tensor constructions and subquotients.
The unfiltered ω_s is constructed without any admissibility assumption. Only its restriction to the admissible generated category and the named tensor group require an admissible pair.
proofSteps: Apply Dieudonné–Manin to each slope summand and take its normalized φ^s-fixed vectors.
Use tensor/dual slope addition and the scalar-extension comparison to prove exactness, faithfulness and the tensor constraints.
Apply s-decency to the representations of G, then neutral Tannaka to the generated subcategory. Keep the full group; identity components are separate.
acceptance: For the trivial object the fibre is Q_{p^s}, not F.
The standard block of slope a/h has fibre dimension h when h divides s.

sources.match: Normalized Frobenius eigenspaces form the finite coefficient fibre functor and decency identifies it with the standard G-fibre.
This is the finite-decent-field crystalline realization; the group convention is corrected to the full group.

nodes.prototype: README: shared isocrystal and tensor-category carriers required

uses.how: Compare its full group with étale full monodromy.

api.name: decentCrystallineFibreFunctor_scalarExtension

api.name: decentCrystallineFibreFunctor_tensor

api.name: decentCrystallineFibreFunctor_decent
api.statement: For s-decent b, ω_s(F_{b,μ}(V))≅V⊗Q_{p^s}, naturally in V and respecting tensors.

api.name: decentCrystallineFibreFunctor_subobject
api.statement: A filtered-isocrystal subobject induces the corresponding injective Q_{p^s}-linear map on fibres.

tests.name: decentFibre_slopeHalf
tests.statement: The rank-two standard isocrystal of slope 1/2 has a two-dimensional ω_2-fibre over Q_{p^2}.

tests.name: decentFibre_scalarRecovery

tests.name: decentFibre_not_naiveFixed

nodes.title: Rank-one coefficient objects and the degree equality
nodes.statement: A rank-one object after scalar extension of the admissible filtered-isocrystal category to Q_{p^s} is represented, up to isomorphism, by integers d_0,…,d_{s-1}, k=Σ_i d_i, an F-basis e_0,…,e_{s-1}, φ(e_i)=e_{i+1} for i<s−1 and φ(e_{s−1})=p^k e_0, with coefficient a acting on e_i by σ^i(a), and filtration jump d_i on K e_i. Conversely these objects are weakly admissible. Inside F_{b,μ}(V)⊗Q_{p^s}, their fibre lines are precisely Q_{p^s}v for v∈V^{s,k}_{b,μ}, allowing all k.
hypotheses: K/F finite and s>0. The scalar-extension category includes the coefficient action, not just a larger ground field.
proofSteps: Decompose the coefficient action using Q_{p^s}⊗F≅F^s. Frobenius cycles its factors; normalize the wraparound scalar by rank-one isocrystal classification.
Each one-dimensional coefficient factor has one filtration jump. Total Hodge and Newton degrees are Σd_i and k.

For the converse, the maximal destabilizing subobject is stable under the coefficient field. A proper nonzero coefficient-stable φ-subobject cannot occur because Frobenius cycles the rank-one factors; hence total degree equality implies weak admissibility.
Identify a map into F_{b,μ}(V) by its first coefficient eigenvector. Strictness of morphisms gives jumps d_i=deg_μ(φ^iv); the two equations are exactly the existence criterion.
acceptance: For s=1 this is t_H=t_N for an ordinary crystalline line.
For s=2, jumps 1 and −1 with k=0 give a rank-one coefficient object; equality of individual jumps is not required.
The same jumps with k=1 fail total degree equality.

sources.match: The cyclic coefficient objects classify rank-one subobjects, and their degree equality gives the explicit invariant-line test.

nodes.title: Chen’s invariant-line criterion for full monodromy
nodes.statement: As closed subgroup schemes of G_{Q_{p^s}}, H_cris,s is the intersection, over all rational representations V, integers k and v∈V^{s,k}_{b,μ}, of the stabilizers of the lines Q_{p^s}v. Consequently any subgroup scheme acting trivially on every such vector is contained in H_cris,s. The stabilizer condition permits nontrivial scalar action on a line.
hypotheses: The admissible pair and finite fibre functor are those of GM0.
The category is closed under subquotients. No connectedness is assumed.
proofSteps: Every tensor automorphism preserves all rank-one coefficient subobjects, so it lies in the stated intersection.

For the reverse containment use Chevalley’s line-stabilizer theorem for H_cris,s over Q_{p^s}. Restrict scalars on its ambient representation and retain the coefficient action to realize this line in the scalar-extended generated category.
Apply coefficient-rank-one to identify the defining line with one of the tested lines. Work functorially over value algebras, rather than equating only rational points.
acceptance: For a torus, preserving a weight line does not require acting as the identity on it.
A finite disconnected algebraic monodromy group is not replaced by the trivial identity component in this criterion.
Use all representations; do not assume every representation embeds in a single mixed tensor power of a faithful one.

sources.match: Chevalley reduces the full tensor group to rank-one coefficient subobjects.
This is the invariant-line formulation used to prove containment of the derived group.

nodes.title: Ambient period comparison and derived containment
nodes.statement: Let H be the full Zariski closure of ξ_{b,μ}(Γ_K), and H_cris,s the full finite-field tensor group. The period Isom^⊗ torsor identifies H⊗B_cris and H_cris,s⊗B_cris by conjugation inside G_{B_cris}, compatibly with the standard fibres. Thus G_der,Q_{p^s}⊆H_cris,s implies G_der⊆H°, the parent Mumford–Tate group. The comparison is for full groups before passing to identity components.
hypotheses: [b]∈B(G,μ) and the bounded period-fibre torsor has the parent’s trivialization.
Both groups use the same generated tensor category under crystalline comparison.
proofSteps: Apply the period comparison isomorphism to all tensor objects and subquotients, producing the fibre-functor torsor and the full-group conjugation.
Its compatibility with the ambient standard G-fibres is essential: G_der is normal in G, so conjugation by the period element preserves it.
Containment descends along the faithfully flat coefficient extensions; connectedness of G_der then places it in H°. An abstract inner-form isomorphism by itself is insufficient.
acceptance: Changing a chosen G-fibre trivialization conjugates both embedded groups.
For G a torus the derived containment is vacuous; no assertion that H is connected is produced.

sources.match: The two fibre functors are compared by their period tensor isomorphism.
Normality supplies the ambient derived-subgroup transfer, with the full/connected correction.

nodes.title: The corrected weighted orbit bound
nodes.statement: Let k=Q_{p^s}, G_k be quasisplit and split over a finite totally ramified extension, and μ be dominant over its finite reflex extension E/k. For a nonzero v∈V_k, let O be any Γ_k-orbit of geometric highest weights occurring in v. Partition O into its distinct Γ_E-orbits C and put q_C=|C|^−1Σ_{λ∈C}λ. For a generic flag η, deg_η(v)≤m_O:=min_C⟨w_0q_C,μ⟩≤Σ_C(|C|/|O|)⟨w_0q_C,μ⟩=⟨w_0λ,bar μ⟩ for λ∈O, where bar μ is the inertia average. The component v_O itself has degree m_O.
hypotheses: The generic-filtration and quasisplit highest-weight contracts in gap G01 are inputs.
Every geometrically occurring highest-weight component of v in O is nonzero by Galois descent. E/k is not assumed normal.
proofSteps: Use the supplier’s generic-filtration identity on k-rational vectors and its isotypic threshold m_O. A vector may meet several isotypic components; its degree is the minimum of their thresholds.
A minimum is at most a convex average. Weight the distinct refined orbits by their sizes; this recombines to the uniform average on O.

Pairing equivariance identifies the full highest-weight orbit average with the inertia average of μ. The splitting field is totally ramified, so the residual unramified action is kept for the next node.
acceptance: For the nonnormal cubic reflex extension of a restriction-of-scalars torus, the refined orbit sizes are 1 and 2; the minimum sees both.
With refined pairings 0 and 3 and sizes 1 and 2, the bound is 0≤2, not an unweighted average of 3/2.
An orbit with repeated refinements is counted once in the partition, even for a Galois reflex field.

sources.match: The degree bound follows from lowest weights and isotypic descent, with all distinct refined orbits replacing the printed automorphism indexing.

nodes.title: The full-period Galois-average inequality
nodes.statement: In the s-decent setup, choose s also so that G_{Q_{p^s}} is quasisplit, b and ν_b are defined there, the based root datum has σ_0^s=1, and the splitting extension is totally ramified. For generic η and every highest weight λ occurring in a nonzero v∈V⊗Q_{p^s}, d_s(v)≤s⟨w_0λ,μ^diamond⟩. Here μ^diamond=(1/s)Σ_{i=0}^{s−1}σ_0^i(bar μ), with repetitions permitted when s is enlarged.
hypotheses: Use a common finite normal closure for all weight/reflex embeddings.
All iterates φ^iv are nonzero and their occurring highest-weight orbits are σ_0^i-translates of those of v.
proofSteps: The factor ρ(b) preserves G-isotypic summands over Q_{p^s}; the semilinear Frobenius transports them by σ_0.
Apply orbit-degree-bound to the transported λ at each iterate and sum.

Move σ_0 across the pairing using its inverse. Only after summing the entire s-period reindex inverse powers to positive powers and identify μ^diamond. This does not assert a termwise positive-power identity.
acceptance: For period two with unequal individual jumps, only their sum is compared with the average.
Enlarging a decency period by a positive multiple multiplies both sides by that multiple.

sources.match: The full Frobenius cycle turns inertia estimates into the Galois-average estimate; reindexing repairs the inverse-action justification.

nodes.title: The Newton lowest-weight inequality
nodes.statement: Suppose ν_b is dominant and v∈V^{s,k}_{b,η}. Every torus weight χ with nonzero component in v has ⟨χ,ν_b⟩=k/s. For every geometric highest weight λ occurring in v one has ⟨w_0λ,ν_b⟩≤k/s.
hypotheses: s>0 and the Newton operator is ρ((sν_b)(p)).
The dominant representative ν_b and the highest weights use the same positive roots.
proofSteps: Extend to a splitting field and decompose v into torus-weight spaces. The p^k-eigenvalue equation forces p^{s⟨χ,ν_b⟩}=p^k on every nonzero component, hence equality of integral exponents.
The lowest weight w_0λ is below each weight χ in its highest-weight summand; pair their positive-root difference with dominant ν_b.
acceptance: For GL_2 with dominant ν=(a,b), a≥b, the standard lowest weight has value b; every eigenvector has slope at least b.
The zero vector would not determine any occurring weight; its exclusion is essential.

sources.match: The Newton eigenvalue fixes occurring slopes and dominance bounds the lowest weight.

nodes.title: Strict Hodge–Newton positivity kills derived weights
nodes.statement: Let Δ be the absolute simple roots, ν≤μ^diamond dominant, and μ^diamond−ν=Σ_{α∈Δ}c_α α∨ with every c_α>0. If λ is dominant and ⟨w_0λ,ν⟩≤q≤⟨w_0λ,μ^diamond⟩, then ⟨λ,α∨⟩=0 for every α∈Δ. Every irreducible of highest weight λ therefore factors through G/G_der. For Δ empty the conclusion about the derived group is vacuous.
hypotheses: All pairings and coefficients are rational; no strict numerical hypothesis is dropped on a simple factor.
The highest-weight representation is over a splitting field of characteristic zero.
proofSteps: Antidominance gives a_α:=⟨w_0λ,α∨⟩≤0. The displayed sandwich gives 0≤Σ c_α a_α≤0. Strict positivity of the coefficients forces every a_α=0.
Apply w_0 to the coroot system and use the supplier’s highest-weight criterion for a representation trivial on the derived group.
acceptance: For SL_2, c>0 and an antidominant nonzero weight give a strict negative pairing, contradicting the sandwich.
If a simple-coroot coefficient is zero, a noncentral weight on that factor need not vanish.
The compact Lean milestone checks the finite positive-sum argument over rational numbers.

sources.locator: End of the proof of Theorem 5.8(2), p. 844
sources.match: Strict positivity of every simple-coroot coefficient forces the occurring irreducibles to be characters.

compactPrototype.name: positive_sum_forces_zero
compactPrototype.scope: Only the finite rational positivity argument; the reductive-group interpretation remains in the document.

nodes.title: Uniform decent-field descent of isocrystal subobjects
nodes.statement: For s-decent b and a rational representation V, every φ-stable F-subspace D′⊆V⊗F is the scalar extension of a Q_{p^s}-subspace of ω_s(V⊗F)=V⊗Q_{p^s}. The descended subspace is stable under ρ(b)σ and under the slope decomposition. In particular every subobject used to test weak admissibility is defined over one common finite coefficient field Q_{p^s}, independent of D′.
hypotheses: s>0 clears the slopes and b,ν_b descend to Q_{p^s}.
proofSteps: Apply the exact finite-field fibre functor to the subisocrystal D′. Its inclusion gives a Q_{p^s}-subspace of the standard fibre.
The scalar-recovery isomorphism recovers D′. Functoriality of the slope decomposition and φ shows stability; no countable enumeration of subobjects is used.
acceptance: For b=1, a φ-stable line is generated by a Q_p-rational vector.
For a slope a/h block with h|s, descent retains its rank and slope rather than replacing it by a rank-one space.

sources.locator: §3.1, pp. 738–740, and proof of Theorem 5.0.6(1), pp. 750–751
sources.match: The finite coefficient fibre functor makes subisocrystals descend uniformly, allowing generic flags to minimize every test degree.

nodes.title: Generic flags minimize subobject Hodge degree
nodes.statement: Let E/Q_p be finite and contain Q_{p^s}, b and the reflex data. For a fixed descended subisocrystal D′, the function x↦t_H(D′_K,Fil_x∩D′_K) on the flag variety Fl_μ/E is upper semicontinuous. Thus if η maps to the generic point, its value is at most the value at any geometric flag x. The total Hodge degree of the ambient representation is constant.
hypotheses: D′ has constant rank and is defined over E. Fil_x is the universal bounded decreasing filtration of type μ.
Hodge degree means Σ_i i·dim gr^i; Newton degree uses v_p(det φ).
proofSteps: Choose uniform bounds A≤i≤B for the filtration jumps. Express t_H as A·rank(D′)+Σ_{i=A+1}^B dim(D′∩Fil_x^i).
Each intersection dimension is upper semicontinuous by determinantal rank loci for the map D′⊗O→(V⊗O)/Fil^i. The finite sum is therefore upper semicontinuous.
An upper closed rank locus containing the generic point contains the integral flag variety; the value there is minimal. Fixed μ fixes the ambient graded ranks.
acceptance: For a filtered plane with jumps 1,0, a fixed line has Hodge degree 1 on its incidence point and 0 on the generic complement.
For the whole plane the Hodge degree remains 1.

sources.match: Generic filtration minimizes Hodge degrees of descended subisocrystals.
The general reductive case uses the same specialization proof after independent nonemptiness.

nodes.title: Generic acceptable decent pairs are admissible
nodes.statement: Let G/Q_p be connected reductive, b∈G(F) decent, [b]∈B(G,μ), K/F finite, and η:Spec K→Fl_μ map to the generic point over the finite reflex field. Then F_{b,η} takes every rational representation to a weakly admissible filtered isocrystal, and hence to an admissible one. This assertion needs no HN-irreducibility.
hypotheses: F=breve Q_p and K contains the reflex field; use the GLX orientation κ(b)=μ^natural and ν_b≤μ^diamond.
Genericity persists under the required finite algebraic coefficient extensions.
proofSteps: Choose a common finite E containing the decency field and reflex data. Descend all subisocrystals using decent-subobject-descent.

Import only part (b) of HS2/nonemptiness-and-period-connectedness, after changing the Berkeley sign by μ↦μ^−1. Its finite classical admissible point is obtained from bounded nonemptiness and does not use this generic-monodromy theorem. Apply HS2/classical-period-points to obtain a weakly admissible flag x.

For each representation and each φ-subobject D′, hodge-degree-specialization gives t_H,η(D′)≤t_H,x(D′)≤t_N(D′). Total equality follows from the fixed Hodge type and admissible-pair invariants. This handles all subobjects without an infinite-intersection argument.
Apply the parent’s perfect-residue-field weakly-admissible/admissible equivalence. The conclusion is the exact tensor functor, not yet a chosen trivialization of the standard-fibre torsor.
acceptance: For a torus there are no flag-incidence variations; total degree equality controls the rank-one cases.
An unstable nongeneric filtered plane can fail weak admissibility even with the correct total degree.
The proof has no edge from the GM4 converse or from an ADLV component classification.

sources.match: The acceptable decent generic pair is admissible; nonemptiness is the additional general-group input.
Specialization proves the subobject inequalities at the generic flag.

nodes.title: Generic monodromy contains the derived group
nodes.statement: Under generic-admissible, suppose μ^diamond−ν_b has strictly positive coefficients on all absolute simple coroots. Then the connected Mumford–Tate group MT(b,η)=H° contains G_der. The theorem holds for arbitrary connected reductive G/Q_p, including ramified and nonquasisplit groups.
hypotheses: b is decent; [b]∈B(G,μ); η is topologically generic over the reflex field.
Fix an enlarged decency period and compatible dominant Newton point as in the estimates. The missing generic-filtration supplier is G01.
proofSteps: Use generic-admissible before constructing the coefficient-line category. Enlarge s so G_{Q_{p^s}} is quasisplit, its splitting extension is totally ramified and all slope/root periods divide s.

Arrange the dominant Newton cocharacter by conjugation defined over a finite algebraic coefficient field. This preserves genericity. Do not claim that arbitrary G(F)-translation preserves a generic flag over the original reflex field.

For every v∈V^{s,k}, frobenius-average-bound and newton-lowest-weight give the sandwich at q=k/s for each occurring λ. strict-hn-forces-central-weight makes each corresponding geometric summand trivial on G_der, so G_der fixes v.
Apply invariant-line-criterion to obtain G_der⊆H_cris,s. ambient-period-transfer gives G_der⊆H° over Q_p.
acceptance: For G=GL_2 and a strictly interior Newton polygon, the connected group contains SL_2.
For a torus the conclusion says 1⊆MT and adds no spurious claim about central monodromy.
If the HN difference vanishes on one simple factor, this argument gives no full derived containment on that factor.

sources.match: The arithmetic estimates and invariant-line criterion force derived containment, without an unramifiedness assumption.

nodes.title: The leading sparse Witt-coordinate term
nodes.statement: Work in the universal p-typical Witt vectors over F_p[X_i,Y_{k,j}], with A_m=Σ_{j≥r}V^j[Y_{m,j}], A_k=Σ_{j≥0}V^j[Y_{k,j}] for k<m, and X=Σ_{i≥0}V^i[X_i]. Write Σ_{k=0}^m A_k X^k=Σ_{n≥0}V^n[P_n], with m>0. For b≤n<bm+r, deg_{X_b}P_n<m p^{n−b}; at n=bm+r its degree is m p^{n−b}, with leading coefficient Y_{m,r}^{p^{bm}}. For n<b the polynomial is independent of X_b.
hypotheses: p is prime; r,b are natural numbers. The degree of zero is treated as minus infinity.
These are Witt coordinates, not coefficients of an ordinary power series.
proofSteps: Lift universal Witt operations to integer polynomial coordinates and apply the n-th ghost polynomial.

Induct on n. Terms from lower Witt coordinates have strictly smaller X_b-degree; at n=bm+r only the leading coefficient of A_m and the m-th power of the b-th variable contribute to the extremal degree.
Reduce the ghost identity modulo p^{n+1}, divide its p^n term, and then reduce modulo p. Keep the factor m outside the exponent: the degree is m·p^{n−b}.
acceptance: For b=r=0, the extremal degree is m and the leading coefficient is Y_{m,0}.
For m=1, r=0, X=V^b[u] and A_1=[a], the b-th coordinate is a^{p^b}u.
The expression m p^{n−b} must not be parsed as p^{n−bm}.

sources.match: The universal Witt-coordinate degree estimate detects a chosen sparse residue digit in an alleged polynomial relation.

nodes.title: Infinite transcendence of the completed unramified field
nodes.statement: For every prime p, F=Frac W(overline F_p)=breve Q_p has infinite transcendence degree over Q_p. Equivalently it contains an algebraically independent sequence indexed by ℕ over Q_p. For every finite E/Q_p embedded in an algebraic closure of F, the finite extension FE/F still contains arbitrarily large finite families algebraically independent over E.
hypotheses: Use the canonical embedding Q_p→F from the complete unramified Witt construction.
The assertion concerns Q_p, not merely Q.
proofSteps: Following Chen, choose Witt vectors x_i supported at factorial digit positions. At a supported position b, use a residue digit of finite-field degree growing like (b^{i+1})!, while previous vectors and earlier digits lie in fields of much smaller degree.

Assume a polynomial relation for x_i over Z_p[x_0,…,x_{i−1}], after clearing coefficient denominators. Let r be the first nonzero Witt digit of its leading coefficient and m its degree. Choose a supported b with no later support through n=bm+r.

Choose a common finite-field degree M for the earlier digits and all coefficient digits through n. Require the new residue degree N to exceed M·m·p^{n−b}; the factorial growth permits this stronger bound, including the factor p^r.
Apply witt-leading-digit: the n-th output digit is a nonzero polynomial of degree m p^{n−b} over F_{p^M} in an element of degree greater than that bound. This contradicts the relation.
Induct to obtain the sequence. Algebraic base extension from Q_p to E does not change transcendence degree, giving the final assertion.
acceptance: A single vector with unbounded residue-field degrees is transcendental, but this alone does not prove a sequence is algebraically independent.
For every fixed flag dimension n, only n independent parameters are needed.

sources.locator: Proposition 2.0.3 and its proof, pp. 734–735; Lemma 2.0.4, pp. 735–737
sources.match: Sparse Witt digits prove infinite transcendence over the p-adic coefficient field; the residue-degree choice is strengthened explicitly.

nodes.title: Generic flags over finite extensions of breve Q_p
nodes.statement: For a finite reflex field E/Q_p and its smooth geometrically integral flag variety Fl_μ/E, there is a finite extension K/F containing E and a map Spec K→Fl_μ whose underlying point is generic. More generally the same assertion holds for a nonempty smooth geometrically integral E-variety.
hypotheses: F=breve Q_p; the embedding E→K is part of the conclusion.
Choose a nonempty affine open and a quasi-compact étale coordinate chart of relative dimension n.
proofSteps: Pass to FE/F finite. Infinite-transcendence supplies n algebraically independent parameters over E, giving a map Spec FE→A_E^n landing at the generic point.
The image of a nonempty étale coordinate chart is open and contains that generic point. Its pullback is therefore a nonempty quasi-compact étale FE-scheme.

By the field-fibre classification it is a finite disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions of FE. Choose one component, with field K. An étale coordinate map preserves the required generic point.
For dimension zero the nonempty integral chart is already finite separable; the argument also covers a torus flag, which is a point.
acceptance: A projective-line flag acquires a point with transcendental affine coordinate over E.
A zero-dimensional flag needs no transcendental parameter.
A merely dense collection of closed points would not give the topologically generic point required by GM2.

sources.match: Étale coordinates and infinite transcendence produce a genuine generic classical flag after a finite extension.
Smooth varieties have étale coordinates; étale maps are open and stable under base change; quasi-compact étale schemes over a field are finite unions of finite separable spectra.

nodes.title: A crystalline period point with open derived image
nodes.statement: Let (G,b,μ) be a local shtuka datum in GLX orientation, with [b]∈B(G,μ) and μ^diamond−ν_b strictly positive on every absolute simple coroot. There are a finite extension K/F containing the reflex field and x∈Gr_μ^b(K) whose crystalline representation ξ_x:Γ_K→G(Q_p) satisfies ξ_x(Γ_K)∩G_der(Q_p) open in G_der(Q_p). No minuscule or quasisplit hypothesis is required.
hypotheses: G is connected reductive over Q_p; F=breve Q_p.
The generic-filtration contract G01 is required by the monodromy theorem.
proofSteps: Replace b by a σ-conjugate decent representative using BG0 and choose a common decency/coefficient field. This replacement is used to construct an open-image point, not to assert arbitrary F-translations preserve genericity.

Use generic-classical-points and generic-admissible to obtain a generic admissible filtration for the decent datum. The bounded parent torsor-triviality theorem produces ξ after choosing its standard-fibre point.
Generic-derived-monodromy gives G_der⊆MT. The parent crystalline-monodromy-group-interface supplies Serre–Sen openness in MT; intersect its open subgroup with G_der(Q_p).
Use HS2/classical-period-points, with the explicit GLX/Berkeley sign dictionary, to lift the admissible flag to the Schubert-cell period point. Transport it back along σ-conjugacy to the original b.
acceptance: The image is compact; openness concerns its intersection with G_der, not equality with a noncompact group.
After any finite extension of K, the restricted image has finite index in the original image and its derived intersection remains open.
For a torus the derived group is trivial and the open-intersection assertion is automatic.

sources.locator: Proposition 5.9 and proof, p. 844; Theorem 5.2, p. 836
sources.match: The generic flag and the parent openness theorem produce the required classical period point.

nodes.title: Open derived image through a z-extension
nodes.statement: Let f:G_tilde→G be a z-extension with central induced-torus kernel. Fix bounded lifted data [b_tilde]∈B(G_tilde,μ_tilde) mapping to [b]∈B(G,μ). Existence of a crystalline period point of this type with open intersection of its Galois image with the rational derived group is equivalent upstairs and downstairs, allowing a finite extension containing the lifted reflex field. This compares existence for the specified lifted data, not arbitrary continuous representations.
hypotheses: Use the common admissible Grassmannian after base change of reflex fields.
The derived morphism G_tilde_der→G_der is a finite central isogeny. It is not asserted surjective on Q_p-points.
proofSteps: The HS2 adjoint period comparison identifies the admissible loci and the extension-of-structure-group torsors. Therefore a downstairs point lifts after finite reflex-field base extension, and the corresponding crystalline representations satisfy f∘ξ_tilde=ξ|Γ_L up to conjugacy.

Let H_tilde and H be full algebraic monodromy groups. Their connected groups satisfy f(H_tilde°)=H° by density and closedness of homomorphism images. An open subgroup of a connected reductive group’s Q_p-points is Zariski dense.

If f(ξ_tilde(Γ_L)) has open derived intersection, H° contains G_der. The algebraic central-lifting contract then forces H_tilde° to contain G_tilde_der. Apply the parent Serre–Sen theorem to ξ_tilde, giving an open derived intersection upstairs.

Conversely the image of an upstairs open derived subgroup is open downstairs because a finite central isogeny in characteristic zero is étale on rational points. Restriction to a finite extension preserves openness by finite index.
acceptance: For SL_2→PGL_2, the rational image is open of finite index; its possible properness does not obstruct openness.
For G_tilde=G×G_m, a central character can change the lift; the conclusion concerns its derived intersection rather than containment of the entire image in G_tilde_der.

sources.locator: Proposition 6.7, crystalline step, p. 851; Proposition 6.6(1), pp. 849–850
sources.match: The period-space identification gives the crystalline lift. Algebraic monodromy and Serre–Sen fill the omitted step about intersection with derived groups.

nodes.title: Compact crystalline-image torsor components
nodes.statement: Let ξ:Γ_K→G(Q_p) be continuous, K/F finite, and let T_ξ→Spd K be its associated locally profinite G(Q_p)-torsor. Put C=ξ(Γ_K), a compact closed subgroup. Choose the convention in which G(Q_p) acts on the geometric fibre on the left and Γ_K acts by right multiplication through ξ. Then π_0(T_ξ)≅G(Q_p)/C equivariantly, and the component indexed by gC has stabilizer gCg^−1. This identifies actual connected components, not an unrestricted orbit quotient for an arbitrary group action.
hypotheses: G(Q_p) has its locally compact totally disconnected point topology.
Use the étale/Galois classification over the analytic field K and its diamond.
proofSteps: Compactness of Γ_K makes C compact and closed. Each geometric Galois orbit gC is compact and descends to a closed subdiamond T_{gC}.

Present C as an inverse limit of finite transitive Γ_K-sets C/U. Their descended finite étale K-covers are connected fields. The qcqs inverse-limit comparison and the spectral clopen criterion show T_{gC} is connected.

Use compactness of C and compact open subgroups of G(Q_p) to separate distinct cosets by C-invariant clopens. Their descended clopens separate distinct orbit subdiamonds, so every T_{gC} is a maximal connected subset.
Compute the left-action stabilizer of gC. No use is made of a universal formula π_0(X/H)=π_0(X)/H.
acceptance: If ξ is trivial, each component is one copy of Spd K and its stabilizer is trivial.
For finite image C, each orbit descends to a finite connected étale K-cover with stabilizer C.
For an infinite compact image, approximate by finite transitive quotients; declaring geometric fibre points to be components would give an incorrect trivial stabilizer.

sources.match: The crystalline torsor’s component stabilizer is its compact Galois image; compact-orbit separation replaces the unrestricted quotient lemma used in the printed proof.

nodes.title: Open derived stabilizers in the ambient tower
nodes.statement: Let y∈Gr_μ^b(K) be an open-derived-image point, T_y its period torsor and j:T_y→Y a G(Q_p)-equivariant map to a locally spatial diamond. Every connected component of Y containing the image of a component of T_y has stabilizer whose intersection with G_der(Q_p) is open. If G(Q_p) acts transitively on π_0(Y), the assertion holds for every component.
hypotheses: K/F finite; all groups and actions have the conventions of compact-torsor-components.
For application to the whole local-shtuka tower, transitivity is a separate geometric supplier assumption.
proofSteps: A continuous map sends a connected component into a connected component. Equivariance includes the source component stabilizer in the target component stabilizer.
Use compact-torsor-components to identify the source stabilizer with a conjugate of ξ_y(Γ_K). Its derived intersection is open by the chosen period point and normality of G_der.
Under the stated transitivity hypothesis every component is a translate of one reached in this way; conjugate the inclusion. Do not infer transitivity merely from connectedness of a quotient.
acceptance: The source stabilizer is equal to the compact image, while the ambient stabilizer is only asserted to contain it.
Without transitivity, the conclusion is restricted to components reached from the torsor.

sources.match: The crystalline-image subgroup embeds into an ambient component stabilizer; the global assertion additionally uses tower-component transitivity.

nodes.title: The quasisplit converse as a component-theorem consumer
nodes.statement: Let G/Q_p be quasisplit, [b]∈B(G,μ), and η an admissible flag over a finite extension K/F for which the standard crystalline-fibre torsor is trivialized. If MT(b,η) contains G_der, then μ^diamond−ν_b is strictly positive on every absolute simple coroot. In particular, for a generic decent pair, derived containment is equivalent to HN-irreducibility once the reverse supplier G02 is available.
hypotheses: The reverse implication (4)⇒(3) of GLX Theorem 6.1(a), with full hypotheses, is the missing independent component/HN-decomposition contract G02.
No quasisplit converse is claimed for arbitrary inner forms.
proofSteps: Apply the parent’s crystalline-monodromy-group-interface to obtain an open intersection ξ(Γ_K)∩G_der(Q_p). No new genericity choice is needed for this implication.

Invoke only the reverse component/HN supplier (existence of such a crystalline representation ⇒ HN-irreducibility). Its proof may use the component argument, HN decomposition and group generation, but must not invoke this converse or the forward generic theorem as a prerequisite of the reverse implication.
Combine with generic-derived-monodromy only to state the final equivalence for generic decent pairs. The forward proof remains entirely in GM0–GM3.
acceptance: The dependency graph has no edge from GM0–GM3 back to GM4.
For a torus the simple-root set is empty; both the derived condition and strict-coroot condition are vacuous.

sources.locator: Proposition 5.11, p. 845; Theorem 6.1(a), equivalence of (3) and (4), p. 845
sources.match: The converse is deduced from the independently proved component/HN characterization of open crystalline derived image.

requests.need: Use the existing scheme-theoretic Chevalley line-stabilizer theorem for a finitely generated Hopf ideal over a field, together with its restriction-of-scalars/representation dictionary. Current Tau Ceti already proves TauCeti.HopfIdeal.exists_finite_subcomodule_exteriorPower_line_stabilizer in Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/ExteriorStabilizer/Character.lean at a91d3aa. Supply the adapter to the generated neutral category when that baseline is adopted; do not replan the line-stabilizer theorem.

For a central torus quotient f:G_tilde→G of connected reductive characteristic-zero groups and a closed subgroup J⊆G_tilde, prove f(J°)⊇G_der ⇒ J°⊇G_tilde_der. Reduce to the inverse image of G_der; its image is reductive, its unipotent radical maps into a torus and hence vanishes, and its derived group maps centrally isogenously to G_der. Also supply rational conjugacy of a rational Newton cocharacter into a chosen dominant chamber after a finite algebraic coefficient extension. These are structure-theory consequences, not new crystalline definitions.

For connected smooth affine groups over Q_p, a nonempty analytic open subset of rational points is Zariski dense. For a characteristic-zero finite central isogeny of semisimple groups, the map on rational points is open onto an open subgroup, with no rational surjectivity assertion. Supply these precise point-topology consequences for the algebraic-monodromy proof of central lifting.

Universal filtrations on the integral flag variety have locally free graded pieces. Determinantal rank loci for D′→V/Fil^i are closed, so dim(D′∩Fil^i) is upper semicontinuous. Also provide nonempty quasi-compact étale coordinates for a smooth integral E-variety, openness/base change of étale maps and the finite separable field-fibre description (Stacks Tags 054L, 02GL, 02GH). Existing SF.0 etale-neighbourhood nodes concern henselization and do not supply these statements.

Specialize the restricted-quotient/component API to a compact subgroup C of a locally profinite rational-point group: G/C is zero dimensional, distinct cosets admit C-invariant clopen separation, and their descended orbit subdiamonds over Spd K are separated by clopens. Combine with the qcqs inverse-limit comparison for finite transitive Galois sets. The existing D5/components-of-restricted-quotients gives only the conditional orbit-space statement; verify the compact separation hypothesis explicitly.

remaining: Adopt the current Chevalley stabilizer through the requested representation/comodule adapter; the rational-period and full-monodromy contracts remain imported from the parent.
Discharge G01 in the owning generic-filtration continuation, including nonnormal reflex-field descent and the full Frobenius orbit contract.
Discharge G01 for derived monodromy; satisfy the SF.0 determinantal-rank request and the structure-layer algebraic-coefficient conjugacy request. Generic admissibility does not require G01.
Discharge the inherited G01 contract for open-image existence; satisfy the étale-coordinate, algebraic central-lifting and rational-point openness requests.

Discharge G02 independently for the converse, the D5 compact-coset separation request, and the inherited forward contracts for open stabilizers. Global transitivity is an explicit hypothesis, supplied geometrically when applying the result to every component.

gaps.title: The generic-filtration supplier has no staged blueprint
gaps.detail: The ReductiveGroupsPartIII restructure proposes ReductiveGroupsLocalGenerationPartII, while RG3.0/highest-weight-character-basis supplies only split geometric highest weights. The required quasisplit descent and generic-filtration contract is not a theorem of RG2.1 or of RG3.0. It must be staged by the owning reductive-group direction. Required contract: for any quasisplit connected reductive k-group in characteristic zero, dominant μ over a finite possibly nonnormal reflex field E/k, the generic filtration V∩∩_{g∈G(E)}gFil_μ is a filtration by G-subrepresentations and equals V∩Fil_η at a topologically generic flag. Its threshold on the k-isotypic orbit O is min over ALL distinct Γ_E-orbits C⊆O of ⟨w_0 average(C),μ⟩. Include equality for conjugate cocharacters after transporting embeddings to a common normal closure, Galois descent of isotypic components with multiplicities, semilinear Frobenius transport, and the character criterion for highest weights annihilating all coroots. These objects stay with that supplier; this roadmap plans only their arithmetic estimates and consumers.

gaps.title: The reverse component/HN supplier is not the staged He21 continuation
gaps.detail: The proposed GLX continuation HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukasPartIIAffineDeligneLusztig has no staged packet. The existing HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukasPartII is the independent He21 dimension direction and cannot supply GLX Theorem 6.1. Required reverse contract: for quasisplit connected reductive G/Q_p and [b]∈B(G,μ), existence over finite K/breve Q_p of a crystalline representation of type (b,μ) with image intersecting G_der(Q_p) openly implies HN-irreducibility. Prove only the (4)⇒(3) direction using the component/HN-decomposition route, independently of its forward generic-monodromy input. The global transitivity used to apply GM4/open-component-stabilizers to every tower component belongs to that geometric direction too; the local application here states it as an explicit hypothesis.

sourceIssues.correction: Use the full closure H for the neutral tensor group and its finite-field crystalline partner. Take H° only when applying the connected Mumford–Tate conclusion, or first restrict to a finite extension killing the finite component group.
sourceIssues.reason: The category of a finite nontrivial representation has a finite nontrivial tensor group, while its connected algebraic monodromy is trivial. Normal connected G_der can still be transferred by the ambient period comparison.

sourceIssues.reason: Take k=Q_5, E=k(cube root of 5), G=Res_{E/k}G_m and V=E. The μ selecting the identity embedding has reflex field E with trivial automorphism group.
